scope: Proposition 14.1 (Retained configurations) of the manuscript “Ordinary two-point correlations of multiplicative functions” (preprints/Ordinary-two-point-correlations-of-multiplicative-functions-September-24-2026/final.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 007 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ccb6f339a7505db7), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 61. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each closed line there is a predicate Rd(nF ) ∈ {0, 1} with the following properties. Whenever it equals one: 1. all core line occurrences are lit; no primitive specification with support contained in F qualifies at a trace vertex; and fewer than t0 repeated center occurrences are unlit; 2. every fixed tree prime has O(Bρ) active components; fewer than B1−2ρ fixed tree primes have more than one active component; 3. fewer than B1−2ρ nonfixed tree primes are corrupted. The implicit constant is uniform in the line. Moreover, X d E  |Kd(n)| ℓ Y j=0 1Y (n + bj)(1 − Rd(nF ))   ≪ exp(−B1+ε/2 ). (14.2) The same exceptional estimates used in this proof remain valid after adding the qualification indicators of at most 2t0 specifications and summing their recorded data, for the classes discarded by an arithmetic saving. Configurations excluded because of a fixed forbidden specification instead vanish with the original Y factors.
